_doc: Per-subcategory scope-selection + read-across config for the Cat-1 compiler. Every number the compiler emits traces to a register row selected by these rules. scope_include/exclude are case-insensitive regex fragments tested against product_scope. read_across names the register row for the nearest analogous government value where no government regulates the exact product. Audited configs for rows 2-9 are filled by the build workflow; formula-powder (row 1) is the regression anchor, calibrated to reproduce the deployed, audited standard.
_panel_note: Full HMTc 11-analyte panel (8 totals Pb/Cd/tAs/tHg/Ni/Sn/Al/Cr + the 3 species iAs/MeHg/Cr-VI). Extended 2026-08-31 from the legacy 8-analyte set (Pb, iAs, tHg, Cd, Cr, Ni, Sn, Al) to add tAs, MeHg and Cr-VI as first-class published cells per the Certification-Readiness Ruling §1 (species bounded by total are enforceable published cells, never blank). MeHg and Cr-VI carry no direct infant-food ML anywhere, so they resolve to `subsumed` (bounded by tHg / total Cr, reflex-enforced) via the compiler's reconcileSpecies pass; iAs is bounded by tAs where the total-As ceiling is stricter (rice subcategories).

_read_across_canon.tAs: in_tas_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_50 — India FSSAI total-As 50 for 'Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods', the strictest sovereign total-arsenic ML for any food intended for infants. Applied uniformly across every Cat-1 subcategory (each is an infant/child food), consistent with the program's existing use of India's infant-foods tin ML (in_sn_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_5000) as the Cat-1 tin read-across. Because iAs ≤ tAs by identity, this 50 also bounds inorganic arsenic: in rice subcategories where the direct iAs ML (100) exceeds 50, the compiler subsumes iAs under tAs (total-As 50 binds, iAs bounded ≤ 50).
_read_across_canon.tHg: china_gb2762_2025_thg_canned_complementary_foods_infants_20 — China GB 2762 total-Hg 20 for canned complementary infant foods; no government sets a mercury ML for these product forms anywhere.
_read_across_canon.MeHg: no direct ML: methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg ≤ tHg) and no jurisdiction sets a MeHg limit for non-fish infant food, so MeHg is subsumed under the binding tHg ceiling (reflex speciation). Fish-containing baby food additionally awaits the Cat-6 species-MeHg read-across decision.
_read_across_canon.Cr: china_gb2762_2025_crtotal_milk_powder_2000 — China GB 2762 total-Cr 2000 for milk powder; dairy read-across. For non-dairy subcategories the nearest analogous Cr source may differ; the workflow adjudicates per subcategory.
_read_across_canon.Cr-VI: no direct ML: subsumed under total Cr (Cr-VI ≤ total Cr), reflex-enforced — any quantifiable Cr-VI fails. Supersedes the prior not-material treatment per the v2.6 species/screens ruling (the species is a published limit-of-record, never a blank cell).

non-root-vegetable-purees.name: Non-root vegetable purees
non-root-vegetable-purees._basis_note: Product is a wet, ready-to-eat non-root vegetable puree (jar/pouch/tub); its physical native basis is as_consumed. native_basis is deliberately set to as_sold because every applicable government limit (EU/UK/IN baby-food MLs, China canned-complementary tHg read-across) is set on this same wet product but tagged basis_class=as_sold in the register, and the compiler's 8:1 powder-reconstitution factor must NOT be applied to any of them. Setting native_basis=as_consumed makes the compiler wrongly divide those wet MLs by 8, inventing six sub-legal numbers (Pb 2.5, iAs 2.5, Cd 5, Ni 63, Sn 630, tHg 2.5) that no government sets. Trade-off: the as_sold setting instead ×8-inflates the one read-across source tagged as_consumed (AU-NZ Al) -> see Al flag.

fish-containing-baby-food.name: Fish-containing baby food
fish-containing-baby-food.scope_note: PROVISIONAL SCAFFOLD, grounded entirely by disclosed read-across (no scope-matched direct). Fish-containing baby food carries two naturally elevated, fish-driven analytes: total mercury (bioaccumulated methylmercury) and total arsenic (predominantly non-toxic organic arsenobetaine). Those two cells take aquatic sovereign limits (total-Hg from the EU fish general ML 500; total-As from the Israel seafood ML 1000), while the non-fish hazards (Pb, Cd, iAs, Ni) take strict infant baby-food ceilings, since a fish baby food is still an infant food and those hazards are not fish-elevated. The toxic inorganic-arsenic fraction stays capped at the infant limit (iAs 20 <= tAs 1000). Methylmercury is bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) for now. OPEN / NOT LOCKED: the fish-specific methylmercury read-across (a species-appropriate MeHg ceiling from the Cat-6 Seafood standard) and the infant-protective-vs-fish-realistic basis for the mercury cell await the Cat-6 species-MeHg read-across decision before this scaffold is promoted to a firm standard.

Pb.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2023/915 lead 20 for baby food and processed cereal-based food for infants and young children. Lead is not a fish-elevated hazard, so the strict infant ceiling governs.

Cd.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2023/915 cadmium 40 for baby food and processed cereal-based food for infants and young children.

iAs.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2023/915 inorganic arsenic 20 for baby food for infants and young children. The toxic inorganic fraction stays infant-capped even though the fish component's TOTAL arsenic is high (organic arsenobetaine); iAs <= tAs holds (20 <= 1000).

Ni.label: government read-across (infant-protective) — EU 2024/1987 nickel 500 for baby food except juices.

tHg.label: government read-across (aquatic) — EU 2023/915 total mercury 500 for muscle meat of fish (general), the fish component's mercury ceiling. PROVISIONAL: pending the Cat-6 species-MeHg read-across decision on whether a fish infant food should carry an infant-protective mercury limit instead.

tAs.label: government read-across (aquatic) — Israel FCS-2016 seafood total-arsenic 1000, reflecting fish's naturally high total arsenic (predominantly non-toxic organic arsenobetaine). The toxic inorganic fraction (iAs) is separately capped at the infant baby-food limit (iAs <= tAs).

_method_note: 8:1 reconstitution applies ONLY to formula subcategories (reconstitution_8to1:true). All other subcategories take government MLs and read-across values at face value. Read-across is always face value (nearest basis-appropriate government row).
_reconciliation_2026_09_02: Round-trip reconciliation against live cert cat1-compiled (docs/tasks/standards-95-confidence-completion-brief.md Phase B): GB 2762-2022 anchors re-pointed to the GB 2762-2025 successors (values unchanged); the eight not-material total-chromium cells now carry the sovereign anchors the live cert records publish (HK Cap 132V cereals 1000 / vegetables 500, GB 2762-2025 cereals 1000); fruit-juice total chromium re-anchored from the NHMRC hexavalent-chromium water row (a species instrument) to the HK total-chromium bottled-water row at the same value; rice-based iAs reproduces the reviewed golden 20 via the EU baby-food read-across. Every published value is unchanged; MeHg and Cr-VI are published as bounded species (subsumed) on all rows.
